articleTitle: Udarata Dance Pose Detection and Validation Using Computer Vision and Deep Neural Networks: A Comparative Study of Static and Dynamic Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Udarata dance, a traditional Sri Lankan art form, requires precise body movements and poses. This research introduces a novel approach for detecting and validating these poses using computer vision and deep neural networks. We explore two methodologies: static pose detection, which compares images against a pre-labeled dataset, and dynamic pose detection, which employs Mediapipe to track body landmarks in videos and an LSTM model to classify sequences of poses as either correct or incorrect. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of these methods in accurately identifying proper Udarata dance poses, offering a valuable tool for dance instruction and cultural preservation. For our experiments, we have defined key angles and heights of body parts and compiled a new Udarata Dance Dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that our algorithms achieve superior performance in pose detection and validation.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Student Learning System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Studies have shown that many students worldwide rely on the internet to study. But the problem arises as most of the sites that provide services to students are limited to some extent or the services are not freely accessible. Therefore, developing an application to combat these issues while minimizing human error and guaranteeing data security is essential. The proposed student learning system has been created to make studying easier with the help of AI powered tools. The AI-powered Student Learning System (AISLS) is designed as an innovative and standalone application aimed at transforming the educational experience for students by integrating with the university Moodle website. Functioning independently, the AI-powered Student Learning System will be accessible through web browsers to provide users with a seamless and intuitive interface for a flexible learning experience. The system assists students to generate study content such as flashcards, summaries, analyze past papers easily with the help of AI-powered technology. Additionally, chatbot assistance, past paper analyzer and external resource curator, it aids in the efficient and effective studying for students with web-based technology. This paper comprehends an attempt to create a web-application to support students to make learning easier by using AI techniques. Finally, a survey was conducted to collect data regarding the quality of the outputs and the user experience.

articleTitle: Real Time Energy Forecasting Scheme for Large-Scale PV Solar Power Plants - Cloud Image Segmentation and Contour Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Solar power is primarily generated through largescale solar power plants. However, several factors can disrupt the output of these plants, with cloud cover being one of the most significant. To predict the effect caused by cloud cover, initially the cloud images should be segmented, and the contour lines of those images should be identified. This part of the study examines multiple algorithms including machine learning and deep learning models to segment the cloud images and detect the contour lines of them. The aim of this part of the study is to test, evaluate, and validate the segmentation and contour identification models to determine the velocity vectors of the clouds. The accuracy of velocity vector patterns is highly relying on the contour lines identified from this approach, making this a crucial step in forecasting cloud movement and its prediction of the outcome of large-scale PV solar power plants under grid 4.0 within the smart grid context.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Features of Indoor Positioning Systems Using Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Explainable AI (XAI) techniques in evaluating the features of indoor positioning systems, with a focus on improving model transparency and interpretability. Indoor positioning systems, crucial for location-based services in complex environments, rely heavily on machine learning models that often operate as black boxes. By performing SHAP (Shapley Additive explanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), this study aims to determine the most influential features by driving model predictions and provide a deeper understanding of their roles within the system. In this study, we investigate the features of RSSI values to check their importance and interactions, enhance the interpretability of the model through SHAP and LIME analyses, and guide future improvements in system accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: A Fully Automated Approach for Enhancing Ancient Tamil Inscriptions Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Ancient Tamil inscriptions hold vast historical knowledge but are often difficult to interpret due to deterioration, posing challenges for archaeologists. Various image processing methods have been proposed to enhance inscription readability, but they require manual tuning, making them not fully automatic, and are unable to restore sections that are damaged or eroded. This study introduces a novel, fully automatic approach that utilizes a Fully Convolutional Neural Network (FCN) for the enhancement of Tamil inscription images. The FCN is trained to generate improved images for enhanced readability, using an annotated dataset consisting of original Tamil inscription images and their corresponding text-segmented masks, annotated by a human expert. To address the challenge of imbalanced foreground and background pixels, where foreground pixels corresponding to annotated text regions are fewer than the background pixels, a class-weighted cross-entropy loss function is employed to train the parameters of the FCN model. The proposed method demonstrates promising applicability, achieving a balanced accuracy of 85% on a dataset comprising 25 Tamil inscription images. This automated approach represents a significant advancement in overcoming the challenges associated with the restoration and interpretation of ancient Tamil inscriptions in the field of archaeology.

articleTitle: Quality Assurance for LLM-Generated Test Cases: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: The rapid advancements in artificial intelligence have transformed software testing, with Large Language Models (LLMs) emerging as powerful tools for automating test case generation. This paper explores Quality Assurance (QA) for LLM-generated test cases in black-box testing through a systematic literature review. Though LLMs are increasingly used for test case generation, challenges in ensuring their quality remain. Following PRISMA guidelines, relevant studies were selected from databases focusing on critical quality attributes, QA frameworks, metrics, and challenges. LLMs demonstrate high efficiency but face numerous issues. A recommendation for future research is given on addressing standardized metrics and improving human-AI collaboration for enhanced testing outcomes.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Machine Learning Approaches for Predicting Wind Power Generation of Thambapavani Wind Farm in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: In recent years, wind energy has become an alternative eco-friendly source of power generation in the Sri Lankan energy landscape. The present study compares machine learning techniques to identify the most suitable wind power prediction model for the Thambapavani Wind Farm, the largest wind farm in Sri Lanka, constructed in 2021. After a comprehensive literature review, three models, namely Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) were selected for this purpose. Wind speed, direction and generation hours with a 10 -minute interval serve as inputs, while wind energy production is the output. The dataset, from May 2021 to December 2023, was collected from the Department of Meteorology and Ceylon Electricity Board, Sri Lanka. The efficiencies of the models were computed using $R^{2}$ and RMSE (Root Mean Square Error) metrics. The accuracies of ANN and MLR models were found 48.35% and $\mathbf{8 2. 7 6 \%}$ respectively, and the experimental results demonstrated that the proposed LSTM model yields the best performance, achieving an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9. 9 9 \%}$. These results provide important clues for improving energy generation methods and boosting the long-term development of energy requirements in Sri Lanka.

articleTitle: Advancing Demand Forecasting for Material Requirements Planning in Food Manufacturing: A Hierarchical Forecasting Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: This study investigates the enhancement of demand forecasting accuracy within Material Requirements Planning (MRP) in the food manufacturing industry by employing hierarchical forecasting. The research evaluates various forecasting models and reconciliation approaches by employing hierarchical forecasting which segments time series data into multiple aggregation levels. The models tested include statistical techniques; autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), exponential smoothing (ETS), prophet and machine learning techniques; linear regression (LR), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector regression (SVR), random forest (RF), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Among the reconciliation approaches; bottom-up, ordinary least squares (OLS), and minimum trace (MinT), Random Forest combined with OLS showed the best performance. A unified forecasting model for total product demand improved accuracy by 20-25% compared to aggregating individual forecasts. These findings underscore the value of advanced forecasting methods in optimizing production planning offering significant practical and academic contributions to the food manufacturing sector.

articleTitle: Enhancing Financial Risk Management with Federated AI
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Fraudulent transactions are a persistent challenge for financial institutions, demanding robust detection systems to maintain customer trust. Key obstacles include the rarity of fraud cases, leading to imbalanced datasets, and strict privacy regulations limiting data sharing. Additionally, fraud detection must be transparent to preserve user trust. This research addresses these issues by combining Federated Learning (FL) and Explainable AI (XAI), allowing institutions to collaboratively train models without sharing data, thus protecting privacy while ensuring model transparency and interpretability.

articleTitle: Handling Data Imbalance in Video Satisfaction Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Video satisfaction analysis could be beneficial for content creators to improve their videos by using comments. Sentiment Analysis (SA) is used to ascertain the sentiment or emotional undertone of a text. In the realm of SA, data imbalance is one of the major problems in SA with Machine Learning (ML) models. This study focuses on comparing the performance of different Sampling Techniques used to address the data imbalance issue with the Sinhala language texts related to video satisfaction. Initially, the study created a labeled dataset with 3680 instances which was created by using YouTube video comments. In this experiment, the performance of seven different Sampling Techniques is investigated. SMOTE, RCSMOTE, ADASYN, Tomek Links, Condensed Nearest Neighbor (CNN) Sampling, NearMiss and SMOTE-Tomek sampling were used as Sampling Techniques for this study. These techniques are evaluated with six different ML models: Naϊve Bayes (NB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Trees (DT), Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost. For individual Sampling Techniques, the Tomek Links undersampling technique performed the highest accuracy at 8 0. 7 0% in the Random Forest (RF) algorithm.

articleTitle: Knee Osteoarthritis Detection Using Machine Learning on Pre-Processed X-ray Images and Treatment Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease marked by the gradual breakdown of cartilage and changes in the underlying bone. The condition is most prevalent in older adults and is often exacerbated by joint injuries and mechanical stress. Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is one of the common disability adjusted life years. There is no cure for the disease, but a combination of lifestyle changes, medications, physical therapies, and sometimes knee transplants can help manage the condition. Despite being time-consuming and highly prone to user variation, manual segmentation, diagnosis, annotation of knee joints, and personalized treatment recommendations remain common procedures for diagnosing osteoarthritis in clinical practice. This research addresses these limitations and reduces diagnostic errors and time and enhance the efficiency and accuracy of knee osteoarthritis diagnosis. The proposed KOA detection model utilizes a deep learning-based approach with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to identified knee joints in x-rays, Binary classification to determine the presence of disease, a pre trained network(VGG16) and custom CNN used to classify the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grades, and random forest model recommending and validating treatment options based on severity. The proposed model has shown promising results by obtaining 98% overall accuracy.

articleTitle: Data Driven Analysis of Protest Dynamics: Comparing Black Lives Matter Movement 2020 and South African Unrest 2021 on Twitter
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Social media has revolutionized public discourse and activism, fostering digital connectivity and engagement. This study explored predictive modelling of protest event signatures on social media, applying machine learning to identify patterns in digital activism discourse. Data from the Black Lives Matter Movement (BLMM 2020) and the South African Unrest (SAU 2021) were analysed to examine temporal dynamics and public engagement on Twitter. Findings from BLMM tweet activity revealed peaks during global solidarity rallies and troughs during police escalations, showcasing significant variability. Similarly, daily tweet volumes during the SAU demonstrated fluctuations in public interest, with spikes linked to pivotal events. The development of a Protest Social Media Archetype further uncovered underlying patterns and similarities across protest movements. This research underscored social media’s role in amplifying marginalized voices, challenging dominant narratives, and mobilizing collective action. By advancing methodological approaches to studying social media data, it provided insights into online discourse during socio-political events. The findings hold implications for academia, policy-making, and activism, advocating for inclusive and participatory digital advocacy strategies.

articleTitle: Development of a Real-Time Hand Gesture Recognition System for Aid of Hearing-Impaired Communication Using Flex Sensors and Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: The word “Gestures” conjures images of persons who are deaf or hearing-impaired. The main reason is that their primary and only mode of communication is based on gestures. Only hearing-impaired people have an understanding of gestures in today’s world. As a result, communicating with regular people has become a challenging chore for them. Consequently, there is a significant communication gap between normal people and those who are hard of hearing. All of this is taken into account, and the purpose of the research is to find a successful solution for hearing-impaired persons to communicate with one another. Here, a glove equipped with flex sensors was used to create a novel real-time gesture detection system based on machine learning. The application of several algorithms, such as the Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Naive Bayes algorithms, might be recognized as a specialty to address this classification problem. The system has been able to achieve a more accurate and precise result by successfully displaying ten messages corresponding to the detected gesture on the Graphical User Interface (GUI). Additionally, this system has the ability to gradually expand the quantity of messages that are communicated by gestures based on the requirements of the users. Due to its wireless connectivity, ease of use, quick response time, and flexibility to meet the user’s demands, this system is probably to become a more popular and beneficial communication aid among individuals with hearing loss in the future.

articleTitle: Nutrient Deficiency Detection System for Black Pepper Leaf using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: This project aims to detect plant nutrient deficiencies in black pepper plants using machine learning algorithms. The system analyzes images of black pepper leaves to identify healthy and unhealthy plants. It uses a wide data set to train the model, labeling plants with specific deficiency symptoms. The system has a user-friendly interface and uses the Xception model of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) as the neural network architecture when implementing machine learning models. Also, the flask is used to implement the backend of the system. TensorFlow in Python is used to train the model. Real-time recommendations and predictions are provided, allowing for adjustments in crop management decisions. This innovative approach helps ensure crop health and productivity. The machine learning model consists of several steps pre-processing including resizing, image rotation and three blur image filters. The accuracy of the Nutrient Deficiency Detection model was $\mathbf{8 9. 4 \%}$.

articleTitle: RSSI-Based Indoor Localization Using Deep Learning with A Custom Loss Function
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep-learning approach for RSSI-based wireless indoor localization by introducing a custom loss function designed to address the unique challenges of RSSI data. The proposed loss function combines logarithmic distance and spatial correlation components, enhancing the model’s ability to predict indoor positions with improved accuracy. The experiment was conducted using generated RSSI data from different anchor nodes, processed in MATLAB. The RSSI values were then trained using neural networks with the proposed loss functions. Experimental results demonstrate the model’s superior performance, confirming the effectiveness of the approach in enhancing localization accuracy and robustness. Key contributions include the development of a specialized loss function and the validation of an advanced deep learning model, providing a foundation for future research to refine the model and test it in real-world environments.

articleTitle: 2D AI Avatar Attributes Impacting on Bank Customers’ Perceived Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: A 2D AI avatar is a digital representation of a human being designed to enhance user interaction in online transactions. Banks especially use this avatar to improve customer experience, engagement, and satisfaction. However, the specific attributes of 2D AI avatars and their effects on customer service experience and satisfaction have not been explored in the existing literature. To address this gap, this study conducted an extensive literature review and developed nine hypotheses to examine these relationships. A quantitative survey was used, targeting a sample of 150 Gen Z bank customers in the Western Province of Sri Lanka. Data analysis was undertaken using SPSS-26 and Smart PLS 4, and the results revealed significant positive relationships between the avatar attributes of likability, credibility, attractiveness, pleasure emotions, dominance emotions, arousal emotions and consumer preferences. And these attributes are also shown to have a positive and significant effect on purchase intention and eWOM. These findings reduce the existing knowledge gap by providing valuable insights to improve online service experience and customer satisfaction in the banking sector through the effective use of 2D AI avatars.

articleTitle: Cross-Platform Topic Analysis: Identifying Trends and Divergences in Social Media Discourse
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: This study carried out an extensive cross-platform analysis of social media discussions related to the Black Lives Matter Movement of 2020.By employing an advanced BERTopic architecture enhanced with RoBERTa based pretrained word embedding’s, key trends and divergences were identified in discussions across Twitter, YouTube, and online news media. The analysis uncovered distinct thematic focuses: Twitter and YouTube prominently highlighted grassroots activism and real-time reactions to events, such as the George Floyd protests, with an emphasis on emotional and personal narratives. In contrast, online news media provided a more structured examination, offering in-depth reporting and objective analysis of the movement’s broader implications. The results revealed significant variations in tone, depth of analysis, and content focus. Twitter and YouTube were characterized by immediate, emotionally charged content and community-driven engagement, whereas news media focused on comprehensive coverage and factual reporting. This cross-platform comparison underscores the diverse roles these media play in shaping public discourse and highlights the importance of engaging with multiple sources for a well-rounded understanding of social justice issues. The study’s findings contribute to a deeper understanding of how different platforms influence and reflect public sentiment and advocacy related to social justice movements.

articleTitle: Optimizing Feature Selection in Spam Email Detection Using Co-Evolutionary Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: The Co-Evolutionary Algorithms for Feature Selections delve into feature selection in the context of data-rich environments. The study aims to identify and implement a suitable co-evolutionary feature selection method for the classification of spam emails. By exploring co-evolutionary algorithms and their application in solving feature selection challenges, the research investigates the transformation of feature selection issues into optimization problems. Through the utilization of co-evolutionary algorithms, the study analyzes and compares the outcomes with other established feature selection methods in machine learning. The findings highlight the effectiveness of co-evolutionary algorithms in feature selection, particularly in the classification of spam emails, showcasing their potential for broader applications in text classification tasks. The paper contributes to the understanding of feature selection methodologies and their practical implications in enhancing classification accuracy and efficiency in data processing tasks.

articleTitle: A Novel Stacked Machine Learning Framework for Enhanced Prediction of Corporate CO2 Emissions in Multisectoral Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Climate change and global warming are among the most pressing issues of our time, drawing worldwide attention due to their observable effects such as extreme weather events, heatwaves, flooding, and droughts. The major driver of these phenomena is the excessive carbon dioxide $\left(\mathbf{C O}_{2}\right)$ emissions into the atmosphere, where corporations play a crucial role. This research aims to accurately predict CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions in the corporate sector. By providing precise predictions, corporations can gain valuable insights to inform decision-making and strategically plan their carbon neutrality initiatives in alignment with sustainability goals. The data used for this research was collected from 17 worldwide companies from 2017 to 2022. This study introduces a novel stacked model that leverages the strengths of four base models: Ridge Regression, XGBoost, CatBoost, and LSTM. A meta-learner, developed using a Random Forest algorithm, aggregates the predictions from these base models. The introduced stacked model significantly outperforms each base model, achieving the lowest MAE and RMSE values and the highest $\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$ of 0.9587, demonstrating superior predictive power. This research contributes to corporate sustainability efforts and offers a wider societal benefit by encouraging reductions in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, ultimately supporting the fight against climate change and protecting the entire ecosystem.

articleTitle: LawKey — Law Constitution Chatbot
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: In response to a pervasive lack of legal awareness among Sri Lanka, this research introduces a law constitution chatbot utilizing Natural Language Processing (NLP). The chatbot is designed to offer precise legal guidance by extracting pertinent laws from the Sri Lankan constitution based on user input. Building on existing studies at the intersection of NLP and the legal domain, this chatbot addresses the lack of relevant legal context for Sri Lanka. Reinforcement learning is integrated to refine the chatbot’s behavior through user feedback, ensuring optimal selection of the most relevant laws. An exploration of applications in countries like Canada and India, where NLP and machine learning have successfully addressed legal information gaps, focuses on various legal domains in Sri Lanka with the aim of empowering the public. The research methodology involves leveraging the Sri Lankan constitution as the dataset, extracting keywords from legal documents, and employing various NLP models, and limitations of the application. A comprehensive literature review reveals the potential energy of NLP techniques in legal chatbots. The global analysis of legal chatbots significantly contributes to the theoretical foundation of this project. In summary, this project seeks to advance legal chatbot technology in Sri Lanka, utilizing NLP and reinforcement learning techniques to empower citizens with legal knowledge and enhance overall legal awareness, thereby addressing the critical issue of legal unawareness and fostering a more informed society.

articleTitle: A Review of Automated Bird Sound Recognition and Analysis in the New AI Era
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Automated bird sound recognition has emerged as a valuable tool for studying and protecting biodiversity. By analyzing bird vocalizations, researchers can gain insights into population dynamics, habitat use, and the impacts of environmental change. This review delves into recent advancements in machine learning techniques, particularly Deep Learning models, for accurate bird species identification. We discuss the challenges and limitations of existing approaches, including data quality issues and the complexity of bird vocalizations. Our analysis highlights the effectiveness of Deep Learning models, such as CNNs and RCNNs, in capturing intricate patterns within bird sounds. By addressing these challenges and leveraging these techniques, automated bird sound recognition systems can provide valuable insights for conservation efforts. Future research should focus on improving model robustness, exploring novel deep-learning architectures, and developing efficient real-time systems to facilitate large-scale monitoring.

articleTitle: Dynamic Ontology-based Travel Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: The growth of personalized travel services calls for sophisticated systems to deliver tailored recommendations based on user preferences and real-time contextual data. The paper presents a Dynamic Ontology-Based Travel Recommendation System that uses semantic web technologies to give personalized travel suggestions. To achieve this, the system has integrated ontology based on travel-related concepts such as destinations, activities, accommodations, and user preferences, facilitating complex querying and reasoning to make recommendations. This is achieved through dynamic content integration, including real-time data updates from external sources and user interactions, making it a responsive system for changing conditions. Moreover, fuzzy matching and ontology merging techniques have been incorporated into the system to effectively deal with uncertainty and combine multiple knowledge sources. Consequently, apart from enhancing the relevance and personalization of travel recommendations, the proposed system also provides explainable suggestions, building user trust and satisfaction.

articleTitle: Hybrid Machine Learning and Moving Target Defense (MTD) for Comprehensive Switchport Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-faceted framework to detect and forestall ARP poisoning attacks in switchport details enhanced by the MTD strategy incorporated with the real-time attack detection system DIPRM under dynamic IP randomization and managed by machine learning to counter new threats. The innovation of this work is the combination of dynamic IP randomization together with ML-based real-time attack detection that creates a strong defense strategy against ARP poisoning, the logical continuation of each static defense avert array, and making a point of the defensive-offensive balance typical for the old-fashioned static security systems. The proposed solution, if applied, exhibited a significant enhancement in addressing ARP poisoning attack identification and prevention aspects, as evinced by the findings on the UNSW-NB15, KDD’Cup99, and NSL-KDD datasets, where the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves of the selected hybrid models outperformed other single algorithmic approaches across precision, recall, and overall net accuracy lines. Consequently, the research study substantiates the efficacy of the discussed hybrid model for eliminating false positives and false negatives conducive to the stability and performance of the network without a significant decline in the system’s throughput.

articleTitle: A Promptable Segmentation Approach to Automatic Floor Plan Analysis using Vision Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Automatic floor plan analysis, rooted in computer vision and pattern recognition, aims to extract critical insights from architectural and interior design drawings, with applications in architecture, real estate, and construction. Conventional methods, whether rule-based or learning-based, face limitations, including extensive manual annotation requirements and challenges in achieving precise segmentation. This research study evaluates the efficacy of Vision Transformers (ViTs) for key floor plan analysis tasks, such as identifying structural elements like doors and windows, extracting line segments to represent room layouts, and segmenting regions like room spaces. We introduce a novel promptable segmentation approach that integrates object detection and image segmentation to achieve a comprehensive understanding of scenes. This methodology centers on the Segment Anything Model (SAM), utilizing input prompts generated by object detection models to guide segmentation. For generating these prompts, we leverage real-time object detection models, such as You Look Only Once Version 8 (YOLOv8) and end-to-end object detection models such as Real-Time Detection Transformer (RT-DETR). Experimental results across diverse datasets demonstrate robust performance, with high Mean Average Precision (mAP), Precision, and Recall rates, setting a new benchmark for automatic floor plan analysis.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Dual-Sensing Smart Waste Management System: Enhancing Urban Cleanliness and Sustainability in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: The management of trash in urban areas encounters substantial obstacles because of the increasing population density and ineffective collection methods, resulting in environmental and health risks in urban cities. Current Internet of Things solutions generally concentrate on monitoring bin fill levels, but fail to include important factors such as garbage decomposing and route optimization. This study presents a novel data-driven artificial intelligence method for garbage management by combining dual-sensing smart bins with real-time analytics. The system we use utilizes ultrasonic sensors to detect the fill-level and methane sensors to monitor spoiling in bins located in Dehiwala, Sri Lanka. The data is transmitted by ESP32 WiFi modules to a cloud-based platform. An individualized Node-RED integration enables the processing of data, while machine learning models enhance the efficiency of collection routes and forecast trends of trash generation. During the pilot implementation involving three smart bins over a four-month duration, the system exhibited several critical capabilities: precise real-time fill-level detection with 95% accuracy, dependable spoilage monitoring with 92% accuracy in methane detection, and effective pattern recognition for weekly and monthly waste generation trends. The route optimization technique demonstrated a 15% enhancement in path efficiency relative to fixed routes during simulation testing. Analysis of temporal patterns identified constant peak fill times and spoiling trends, facilitating predictive scheduling possibilities. This study demonstrates the capacity of data-driven intelligence formulate a paradigm for scalable intelligent waste management systems, showcasing the potential for biogas system integration and adaptive capacity planning.

articleTitle: Cluster-Based Time Series Modelling and Forecasting of Mobile Network Traffic
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: In the ever-evolving digital age, advancements in communication and network technologies have revolutionized the digital way of interaction, which is driven by the rapid evolution of cellular networks. With the continuous improvements in the mobile network generations, a vast number of devices have emerged in recent years. In the meantime, the high volume of cellular traffic demands enhanced, reliable, and streamlined services. Addressing these growing demands requires an effective way of a proactive approach to allocating cellular network resources. One of the most important components of the network resource allocation management system is the forecast of network traffic, which is highly complicated in terms of accuracy and reliability. This study presents a cluster-based approach, known as within-cluster sum of squares (WCSS), using K-means clustering algorithms to aggregate the data points from the real-world Call Detail Records(CDR) dataset that uncover similar patterns of internet traffic. This approach allows for the creation of a more organized and consistent analysis process, leading to more accurate forecast of network traffic. The selected time series models of ARIMA, SARIMA, and LSTM were employed in the clustered dataset and evaluated against error metrics of MSE, RMSE, and MAE. A comparative analysis of internet traffic forecasting models showed that ARIMA outperformed both SARIMA and LSTM in terms of accuracy. The findings of the study mark a promising step, by introducing the cluster-based approach for time series analysis of mobile Internet traffic.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis with Support Vector Machines for Travel Agency Ranking and Traveler Decision Support in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Travelers often rely on online reviews to plan trips, but the large volume of data can hinder informed decision-making, especially in the Sri Lankan tourism industry. This research develops a sentiment analysis-based system to help travelers navigate reviews and make informed choices. The system uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to preprocess and structure user reviews, categorizing them into subcategories like transportation, accommodation, food and beverage, entertainment, recommendations, purpose, and travel agencys. Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Multinomial Naive Bayes (MultinomialNB) classifiers are employed to assess sentiment, classifying reviews as positive, neutral, or negative. The integration of NLP and SVM ensures high accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability in sentiment analysis, enhancing the model’s performance. The designed platform presents travelers with an easy-to-understand bar chart summarizing travel agency reviews and providing actionable insights into service quality. Key metrics like precision, recall, and score validate the model’s effectiveness. By organizing feedback into insights, the system empowers travelers to make better decisions and helps travel agencies identify areas for improvement. The scalable approach allows for adaptation to larger datasets and various tourism contexts, making it a reliable tool for comparing Sri Lankan travel agencies and improving the overall tourism experience.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of machine learning models for Breast Cancer Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Recently, large-scale data merging and ensemble learning algorithms have emerged as promising approaches to breast cancer prediction and classification. Computer-aided detection and diagnosis technology can help people live longer by facilitating early detection of breast cancer. Aberrant cell division in the breast is the primary cause of breast cancer, which can develop into either a benign or malignant tumor. Because of this, early detection of breast cancer is essential, and many lives can be spared with effective treatment. The results and assessments of several machine learning models for detecting breast cancer are covered in this study. The approach was developed using the Wisconsin Breast Cancer Diagnostic (WBCD) dataset. The dataset has some intriguing data even though it is small. The data was examined and utilized in several machine learning models. Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Neighbors Classifier (KNN), Naïve Bias model, Logistic Regression (LR), AdoBoost and Decision Tree (DT) were used for prediction. It is discovered that the AdoBoost model produces the best results when the results are compared. $96 \%$ accuracy and logistic regression model is predicted $96 \%$ of ROC value. Logistic regression model and AdoBoost, which is better than the previously published approach.

articleTitle: Enhanced Failure Detection in Induction Motors Using Supervised Learning and Data Smoothing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Production machinery failures often cause significant financial losses, and traditional maintenance methods may struggle to mitigate these issues effectively. Predictive maintenance offers a modern solution by forecasting failures before they occur. This study applies supervised learning algorithms to pre-collected vibration data from a single-phase induction motor under normal and simulated abnormal working conditions. Data smoothing techniques such as Moving Average Filter, Kalman Filter, and FFT were employed to enhance data quality. Supervised algorithms including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, SVM, Naive Bayes, and kNN were implemented and evaluated. Performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score were used to compare these algorithms. Results indicate that data smoothing significantly improves model performance, with the Moving Average Filter achieving the highest accuracy for Random Forest at $\mathbf{9 9. 7 7 \%}$. These findings highlight the potential of advanced machine learning techniques combined with data preprocessing for predictive maintenance in industrial settings. By reducing downtime and maintenance costs, these models enhance operational reliability and efficiency. This study contributes to the growing knowledge on applying machine learning for predictive maintenance, offering practical insights for improving the sustainability and productivity of manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: Optimizing Production Efficiency in the Garment Industry: The Role of Predictive Analytics Techniques in Sri Lanka’s Textile Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: This research explores the significant role of predictive analytics in optimizing production efficiency within Sri Lanka’s garment industry, a key contributor to the nation’s economy. The study synthesizes current knowledge on predictive analytics, focusing on its application in improving operational decision-making and addressing challenges related to data requirements and preprocessing in garment manufacturing. Through a systematic literature review, 30 relevant studies were identified and analyzed, highlighting key factors influencing production efficiency, such as labor management, Standard Minute Value (SMV), work-in-progress (WIP), and overtime. The research underscores the potential of advanced predictive techniques like ensemble models to drive operational improvements. However, it also identifies significant challenges, particularly the reliance on short-term datasets, which limit the ability to capture seasonal patterns crucial for accurate production forecasting. The study advocates for the development of multimodel frameworks and the integration of time series analysis to enhance predictive accuracy and decision-making in the garment industry. By adopting these advanced methodologies, the industry can better navigate the complexities of production processes, ultimately improving efficiency and competitiveness in the global market.

articleTitle: Analyze Factors Affecting Thread Consumption in a Garment and Develop a Machine Learning-based Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: The garment manufacturing industry faces challenges related to excess thread stock, leading to increased write-off expenses and environmental impact. This research utilizes Machine Learning (ML) techniques to predict sewing thread consumption in producing full underwear briefs, considering key factors such as garment style, fabric/seam thickness, stitch length, seam type, and estimated wastage. Multiple ML models, including Linear Regression, Ensemble Models (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), were employed to predict thread consumption for two thread types (TKT 120 and TKT 160). These models are integrated into a user-friendly Streamlit interface to make real-time predictions based on user input, improving inventory management decision-making. ANN models outperformed others, with a validation dataset MAPE of $\mathbf{1. 2 1 \%}$ for TKT 120 and $1.99 \%$ for TKT 160. This study shows how ML optimises thread usage, reduces inventory costs, and supports garment manufacturing sustainability. The ANN model performs well, but refinement and feature exploration could improve prediction accuracy and generalization. The research emphasises ML and usercentric tools for industry resource management efficiency.

articleTitle: PaddyShield: A CNN-Based Rice Leaf Diseases Detection and Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Sri Lankan paddy farmers face numerous challenges due to limited access to resources and knowledge of pests and diseases effectively. This often leads to wasting money on pesticides without addressing the problem, affecting crop yield. Existing systems excel at swift disease detection but do not acknowledge farmers in preventing and mitigating diseases. Farmers expect information on the diseases and suitable mechanisms to get rid of the diseases. Further, we conducted a pre-survey with paddy farmers in the Anuradhapura district. We understood the importance of acknowledging the pests and diseases and the methods to mitigate them. Therefore, we developed a “PaddyShield” system to identify diseases and provide comprehensive disease details on prevention mechanisms for the identified diseases through rice leaf. The “PaddyShield” system was implemented after employing the sophisticated Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) as the linchpin for precise disease detection. The system’s strength lies in its adept handling of a diverse dataset encompassing various paddy leaf diseases, ensuring accuracy ($\mathbf{9 5 \%}$) in early disease identification. Through rigorous testing, the system indisputably highlights its superiority over existing solutions. Accessibility is prioritized through a user-friendly Flaskpowered interface. Overcoming hurdles like data preprocessing and model complexity with inventive solutions, the system achieves seamless backend-frontend integration. Optimal GPU resource utilization further accentuates its efficiency.

articleTitle: 1D CNN-Based Traditional Instrument Classification and Notation Generation in Sinhala for Gataberaya and Flute
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Applications for traditional musical instruments from Sri Lanka have not received enough attention, even with the progress in machine learning. This paper presents a novel method for categorizing and transcribing notations for the flute and gataberaya which is an indigenous drum from Sri Lanka using deep learning methods. Based on a manually recorded audio recording dataset with 168 flute recordings and 81 gataberaya recordings with varying lengths and single-noted, 1D Convolutional Neural Networks were used to construct a classification model. The system also generates musical notations from audio recordings using an algorithm and converts Western musical notation to Sinhala musical notations using a prompt with a Large Language Model API call. The methodology includes data augmentation for raw data and feature extraction with Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients, and frequency analysis using the Fast Fourier Transform. The classification model achieved 88.71% training accuracy and 91.16% validation accuracy, successfully identifying instrument types, and the notation generation for the flute shows effectiveness by correctly recognizing the notes and the relative octave of the frequency. However, challenges remain for unpitched instruments like the Gataberaya due to the limited dataset. This approach acts as a valuable tool for the preservation of Sri Lankan traditional music.

articleTitle: Automated Algae Detection and Quantification on Coral Reefs Using U-Net Segmentation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Coral reefs, essential marine ecosystems, face increasing threats from algae overgrowth, leading to coral bleaching and ecological imbalances. Efficient monitoring and quantification of algae presence are crucial for coral conservation. This study introduces a segmentation model leveraging the U-Net architecture to detect and quantify algae coverage on coral reefs. The model was trained on a custom dataset created using underwater videos provided by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). Extracted samples underwent pre-processing and data augmentation to enhance the dataset’s diversity and size. The proposed segmentation model achieved satisfactory accuracy, with a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of $\mathbf{0. 8 5}$, indicating reliable accuracy in distinguishing algae and coral. This level of accuracy enables practical use in conservation efforts, offering a competitive advantage over traditional manual monitoring methods. Segmentation results were further processed to calculate the percentage coverage of algae overlapped on coral using an image processing technique. The model’s output is designed for integration into a mobile application, providing field researchers and marine enthusiasts with real-time analysis and quantification of algae coverage. The research signifies a substantial advancement in the application of deep learning techniques for environmental monitoring, contributing significantly to marine biodiversity preservation efforts.

articleTitle: Exploring Mind Models: A Comparative Study as the Inaugural Step Towards Consciousness Chatbots
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Exploring how our minds work is essential to grasp human thoughts. This study delves into why studying these models matters, forming the basis for creating chatbots that mimic human conversations. It ventures into philosophy, psychology, and technology, navigating the changing landscape of mind understanding while keeping ethics and privacy in focus. The study starts by breaking down popular models of personality assessments, including the DISC Model, Enneagram, Big Five, MBTI, Holland Code, and the fascinating Dark Triad. After that, it explores sentiment analysis, social media data, and psycholinguistics models like LIWC, giving a thorough rundown of the techniques used. The research delves deeper into this rapidly developing topic to better understand conversational agents’ and chatbots’ potential to understand human preferences, concerns, and communication patterns. Additionally, this emphasizes the value of user privacy and ethical issues, highlighting the possibility of people changing for the better. This aims to present a new viewpoint drawn from Buddhism that, although it does not strictly classify the mind, provides insightful knowledge about human nature and consciousness. By highlighting the holistic and ethical aspects of this diverse discipline and conforming to the dynamic subtleties of human cognition, the study advances the continual improvement of mind models.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning based Warehouse Task Assignment
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: The rise of e-commerce demands greater efficiency in warehouses, requiring dynamic task allocation among humans and robots. Traditional methods often fail in such complex environments. This research introduces a MultiAgent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize task assignments. The model considers detailed task and device attributes like type, urgency, and availability. Agents use Deep Q-Networks (DQNs) to make informed decisions based on perceived warehouse state. A carefully designed reward system prioritizes timely order completion and efficient task execution. Simulations show significant improvements in efficiency, especially in pick task completion and device use. The results confirm MARL’s potential for optimizing warehouse operations.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Multilingual Language Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Multilingual language translation is a crucial undertaking in herbal language processing (NLP), facilitating pass-linguistic verbal exchange and know-how. Existing deep getting to know models, including Transformers, Multilingual BERT (mBERT), and mBART, have proven sizable advancements in translation satisfactory; however, they come with boundaries. Standard Transformers and mBERT models regularly struggle with low-resource languages and 0-shot translation situations because of their reliance on substantial parallel corpora or confined language representation. To cope with those drawbacks, a singular method is proposed that mixes the strengths of the mBART and M2M-100 architectures. This method leverages a hybrid version structure incorporating a chain-to-sequence Transformer framework more suitable with go-lingual switch mastering and information augmentation techniques. The approach allows higher performance in low-aid language settings and extra correct translations across non-English language pairs. The proposed methodology entails pre-education on a diverse set of multilingual datasets accompanied by using pleasant-tuning with augmented low-useful resource language records. Experimental consequences display that this model outperforms current fashions like mBART and M2M-100 via 12% in BLEU ratings for low-resource languages and achieves trendy performance in many-to-many translation duties. Additionally, the model well-known shows more suitable efficiency and scalability, making it suitable for real-world multilingual applications. This research contributes to the development of extra sturdy and efficient multilingual translation systems, paving the way for stepped forward movelingual verbal exchange in numerous international contexts.

articleTitle: Enhancing Small Dataset Classification Using Projected Quantum Kernels with Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have shown promising results in efficiency and accuracy in image classification. However, their efficacy often relies on large, labeled datasets, posing challenges for applications with limited data availability. Our research addresses these challenges by introducing an innovative approach that leverages projected quantum kernels (PQK) to enhance feature extraction for CNNs, specifically tailored for small datasets. Projected quantum kernels, derived from quantum computing principles, offer a promising avenue for capturing complex patterns and intricate data structures that traditional CNNs might miss. By incorporating these kernels into the feature extraction process, we improved the representational ability of CNNs. Our experiments demonstrated that, with 1000 training samples, the PQK-enhanced CNN achieved 95% accuracy on the MNIST dataset and 90% on the CIFAR-10 dataset, significantly outperforming the classical CNN, which achieved only 60% and 12% accuracy on the respective datasets. This research reveals the potential of quantum computing in overcoming data scarcity issues in machine learning and paves the way for future exploration of quantum-assisted neural networks, suggesting that projected quantum kernels can serve as a powerful approach for enhancing CNN-based classification in data-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Implementing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy in Chatbots to Reduce Students’ Exam Stress using ChatGPT
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Undergraduate students frequently encounter academic stress, highlighting the need for accessible and effective coping mechanisms. This study develops an AI chatbot grounded in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) principles to meet the mental health needs of these students. The primary goal is to devise and assess a chatbot that delivers personalized support for managing academic stress. The chatbot engages students in meaningful conversations, identifies cognitive distortions in their thought processes, and provides customized coping strategies. It leverages OpenAI’s GPT-3.5 turbo LLM for generating lifelike interactions and uses a vector database to store domain-specific knowledge. Responses are preprocessed with OpenAI embeddings for intent classification. Support Vector Machines (SVM), Multinomial Logistic Regression, and Random Forest models are used for classifying cognitive distortions, with SVM achieving the highest accuracy of $85.94 \%$. Intent classification is refined using cosine similarity, enhancing the chatbot’s conversational accuracy. Although SVM outperforms other models, ongoing challenges call for further research to refine the chatbot’s functionality and improve its impact on student well-being.

articleTitle: Enhancing Perception for Autonomous Driving Systems with Dual-Vision Input Cycle GAN for Night-to-Day Image Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Autonomous Driving Systems (ADS) and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) heavily rely on vision-based data for critical decision-making. However, these systems face significant performance limitations in low-light conditions where conventional RGB vision inputs struggle to capture information due to low light. Current solutions, including high-gain cameras or LiDAR-based approaches, are expensive and increase system complexity. This study presents a novel approach to address these challenges by employing a night-to-day image translation model with modified CycleGAN. The proposed model translates RGB and infrared (IR) inputs into a daytime representation, enhancing overall perception and object detection in low-light scenarios. Unlike existing methods, the model operates in an unsupervised learning framework, avoiding the need for large, paired datasets, which are often difficult to obtain. The study also introduces architectural modifications to the CycleGAN, including a dualinput framework and refined architecture, to optimize performance across varied conditions. The model’s performance is demonstrated through reference-less evaluation metrics, achieving average scores of FID 8.04, NIQE 4.92, and BRISQUE 36.3. These results illustrate the potential of the model to enhance the safety and operational stability of autonomous driving systems in low-light environments.

articleTitle: Development of a Computationally Efficient CNN-Based Deep Learning Model for Anomaly Detection in Retail Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: The retail industry experiences significant financial losses annually due to inventory shrinkage caused by shoplifting. Resource constrained retail environments face significant challenges in detecting anomalous behaviors such as shoplifting due to the high computational demands of advanced anomaly detection systems. These limitations highlight the need for computationally efficient solutions tailored to the specific challenges of such settings. This study introduces a computationally efficient anomaly detection model using a DenseNet121-based convolutional neural network architecture, specifically designed for resource-constrained retail environments. The model was trained and tested on the UCF-Crime dataset, which includes a variety of suspicious and normal activities, to enhance the detection of abnormal behaviors such as shoplifting. By prioritizing reduced computational complexity without sacrificing detection accuracy, our approach achieves a detection accuracy of 68% with an AUC score of 0.65, making it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings such as small retail operations. Compared to more complex models like 3D CNNs which achieve $\mathbf{7 5 \%}$ accuracy and an AUC of 0.72 and YOLOv5, which achieves 92% accuracy and an AUC of 0.80, the proposed approach significantly lowers computational demands, making it suitable for real-time deployment in small retail operations. This provides a practical solution for improving security in retail contexts. This research represents a novel step toward accessible and efficient retail surveillance, with the potential to reduce theft-related losses. Future work will focus on addressing class imbalance and improving the detection of complex behaviors.

articleTitle: Review on AI Assistant Systems for Programming Language Learning in Learning Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 8th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has made it possible to improve student engagement in the learning environment in many ways, including fusing the adaptive, individualized support of AI assistants with the motivating elements of gamification. The study examined the range of AI-powered platforms and tools that include gamification components, including AI-powered code generation aids, adaptive feedback mechanisms, and intelligent tutoring systems. These technologies meet the varied needs of students, which improves retention and comprehension, in addition to making learning more engaging and participatory. The paper also emphasizes how an AI-enabled gamified environment may facilitate group learning and help students gain a deeper comprehension of challenging programming concepts. However, it also discusses the difficulties and moral issues surrounding the application of AI in education such as loneliness, less student interaction, low motivation, etc, highlighting the necessity of cautious application and ongoing assessment. The review’s conclusions indicate that gamified learning environments with AI capabilities have great potential to transform programming education and give students a more effective, customized, and interesting learning experience.
